name: map-catalog
prompt: The city archive keeps two catalogs of historical maps. The paper catalog records the year of each survey, while the digital catalog records when a scan was uploaded. These dates answer different questions. In April, a volunteer scanned several nineteenth-century maps, including one surveyed in 1848 and another surveyed in 1872. Both scans were uploaded on the same afternoon. The curator asked for a display ordered by survey year, with the earliest survey first. A draft display accidentally sorted by upload time; because the scans shared an upload date, it placed them in filename order instead. The volunteer noticed the mistake before visitors arrived. She checked the handwriting on the original sheets, confirmed the survey years against the paper catalog, and corrected the display labels. The archive kept the upload dates in a separate technical log for preservation staff. No survey year was inferred from the scan filename or from the day the images were copied to a backup drive. Write a concise caption explaining which map should appear first and why.
